newsitem.title: USA: Western Resources opposes ADT's 'poison pill'.
newsitem.headline: Western Resources opposes ADT's 'poison pill'.

text.p: Western Resources Inc said Tuesday it filed an amended complaint in an attempt to invalidate ADT Ltd's anti-takeover or "poison pill" provisions.
Earlier this month, ADT rejected a $3.5 billion, or $22.50 a share, takeover bid. Western Resources is ADT's largest shareholder.
Western Resources said it filed its amended complaint in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida.

Western Resources said it opposes ADT's "poison pill" amendments, which it called "dead hand provisions." These provisions, it said, would attempt to preserve the current ADT board members' right to redeem the plan even if they were voted out of office.
Western Resources said it believes the poison pill provisions represent an attempt by ADT to "interfere" with the shareholder vote on Western Resources' proposal to replace the ADT board.

"Our view is that these 'dead hand' provisions are invalid because they serve no purpose but to entrench management and, consequently, infringe on the rights of shareowners," John Hayes Jr., Western Resources chairman, said in a statement.
Western Resources holds about 27 percent of the ADT common shares.
